title: IndustriAll Europe union protest at European Parliament in Strasbourg

tea.why: Metal and textile workers are protesting against job insecurity, layoffs, wage struggles, and industry shifts toward defense.
tea.want: Protesters demand favorable conditions within the upcoming Industrial Accelerator Act to protect and revive European industry.
tea.changed: Nov 24, 2026: IndustriAll Europe members and metal and textile union delegates demonstrated outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg.

summary: On November 24, 2026, metal and textile workers and union delegates gathered outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, for a large mobilization organized by IndustriAll Europe. Participants, including delegations from unions like ACV-CSC METEA and various industrial sectors, traveled by bus to voice concerns over job losses, layoffs, reliance on state support schemes, and fears that corporate investments in the defense sector might harm traditional civilian manufacturing. The demonstration took place ahead of the formulation of the Industrial Accelerator Act, with participants calling for protective regulations and favorable conditions for the continent's industrial sector.
demands: Favorable conditions in the Industrial Accelerator Act
Safeguard manufacturing jobs against foreign competition and shifts to defense
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Delegates and workers from various industrial sectors demonstrated outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg, organized by IndustriAll Europe.
